lesson: For high-growth tech/semis, always pull customer concentration percentages from 10-K filings rather than using qualitative language, since this is a recurring material risk factor
When citing forward-looking supply/demand claims (e.g., 'sold out through X year'), flag single-source news items distinctly from financial-statement-backed facts
For high-beta, high-multiple AI stocks, pair beta/volatility stats with options-market signals (IV, skew) for a fuller two-sided risk picture
Always attempt to pull segment-level revenue breakdown for diversified tech companies to assess true concentration vs. headline growth narrative
Explicitly define and apply a sentiment scoring methodology before labeling aggregate news sentiment as neutral/positive/negative to avoid unsupported editorializing
For mega-cap AI/semis, always pull segment-level margin detail (not just consolidated gross margin) to explain compression/expansion drivers
Treat options volume figures as neutral data points unless open interest or skew data confirms directional bias—avoid labeling raw volume as 'bearish'
For companies with customer concentration risk disclosed qualitatively, search filings for the specific revenue percentage by named customer if available
When macro 10Y yield and Fed funds diverge sharply, flag the yield curve dynamic explicitly as a distinct macro risk factor separate from rate-cut narrative
Always add at least one direct peer valuation comparison for high-multiple growth stocks to anchor whether current multiples are historically/competitively stretched
